title: Subdomain Discovered
description: A subdomain belonging to the target organisation was identified through passive or active enumeration (Amass, subfinder, certificate transparency, theHarvester, puredns brute-force).
remediation: Review all discovered subdomains for unintended exposure. Ensure internal/development subdomains are not publicly resolvable where unnecessary.

title: Live Host Confirmed
description: A subdomain or IP address responded to HTTP/HTTPS probing (httpx) or ICMP/TCP and is confirmed to be serving traffic.
remediation: Ensure only intended services are publicly accessible. Review the confirmed host list for shadow IT or forgotten assets.

title: Open Port Identified on Subdomain
description: A non-standard or sensitive port (e.g., 8080, 8443, 9200, 27017, 3306) was found open on a subdomain via naabu port scanning or Shodan. Exposes additional attack surface.
remediation: Restrict open ports to those strictly required. Apply firewall rules to limit access to sensitive ports (databases, admin panels) by source IP.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate Expiring Soon
description: An SSL/TLS certificate for a discovered host will expire within 30 days. Expiry causes browser security warnings and can disrupt services.
remediation: Renew the certificate before expiry. Implement automated certificate renewal (e.g., Let's Encrypt with certbot/acme.sh).

title: SSL/TLS Certificate Already Expired
description: The SSL/TLS certificate for a discovered host is expired. Browsers will display security errors; automated clients may reject connections.
remediation: Renew the certificate immediately. Review certificate lifecycle management procedures.

title: SSL/TLS Certificate Misconfiguration
description: A certificate was found with a misconfiguration: hostname mismatch, self-signed cert on a public host, wildcard overuse, or weak signing algorithm (MD5/SHA-1).
remediation: Replace self-signed or mis-issued certificates with certificates from a trusted CA. Use SHA-256 or stronger signing algorithms.

title: DNS Misconfiguration
description: A DNS record anomaly was detected: dangling CNAME, multiple conflicting A records, DNSSEC misconfiguration, or inconsistent NS delegation that could be exploited.
remediation: Audit DNS records for the affected domain. Remove stale or dangling records. Ensure DNSSEC is correctly signed and validated.

title: SPF Record Missing
description: No SPF (Sender Policy Framework) TXT record was found for the target domain. Without SPF, attackers can spoof email from this domain and bypass basic spam filters.
remediation: Add an SPF TXT record to the domain's DNS: e.g., v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all. Consult your mail provider's documentation.

title: DMARC Record Missing
description: No DMARC (_dmarc.<domain> TXT) record was found. Without DMARC, there is no policy instructing receiving mail servers how to handle unauthenticated email from this domain.
remediation: Add a DMARC record starting with p=quarantine or p=reject. Example: v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com

title: DKIM Configuration Missing
description: No DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) selector was discoverable for the target domain. Without DKIM, email authentication is weaker and phishing risk increases.
remediation: Configure DKIM signing on your mail server and publish the public key as a DNS TXT record under <selector>._domainkey.<domain>.

title: Breached Email Address Found
description: An email address associated with the target organisation appeared in a known data breach (HIBP or Dehashed). The account holder's credentials may have been exposed.
remediation: Notify affected employees. Force password resets for all affected accounts. Enable MFA. Review whether compromised accounts have access to sensitive systems.

title: Plaintext Credential Found in Breach Database
description: A plaintext or reversibly hashed password was found in a breach database (Dehashed) for a target-domain email address. Direct account compromise may be possible.
remediation: Immediately force a password reset for the affected account. Check for reuse across other systems (VPN, cloud consoles, O365). Enable MFA on all accounts.

title: GitHub Secret / API Key Exposed
description: GitDorker or TruffleHog identified a secret, API key, token, or private key in a public GitHub repository associated with the target organisation or its employees.
remediation: Revoke the exposed secret immediately. Rotate all affected credentials. Scrub the secret from git history (git filter-repo). Enable GitHub secret scanning alerts.

title: M365 Valid User Enumerated
description: TREVORspray or Azure AD authentication confirmed that a discovered email address is a valid M365/Azure AD account (user exists in the tenant). Confirms the account is a viable spray target.
remediation: Enable account lockout and smart lockout in Azure AD. Implement Conditional Access policies. Consider disabling legacy authentication protocols.

title: M365 Valid Credential Found (Credential Spray Success)
description: TREVORspray successfully authenticated to M365/Azure AD with a discovered credential. Full account access to Microsoft cloud services may be available to an attacker.
remediation: Immediately revoke the session, reset the password, and enable MFA for the compromised account. Investigate access logs for lateral movement. Review Conditional Access policies.

title: Subdomain Takeover Risk
description: A subdomain has a CNAME pointing to an external service (e.g., GitHub Pages, S3, Heroku, Shopify) that is no longer claimed. An attacker could register the resource and serve malicious content under the organisation's subdomain.
remediation: Remove the dangling DNS record immediately. If the external service is still needed, reclaim the resource. Implement subdomain monitoring.

title: DNS Zone Transfer Allowed
description: A nameserver for the target domain accepted a DNS AXFR (zone transfer) request from an unauthenticated source. This exposes the complete DNS zone — all hostnames, IPs, and internal network topology.
remediation: Restrict zone transfers to authorised secondary nameservers only (ACLs on the primary NS). Most modern DNS servers disable AXFR by default — verify configuration.

title: Employee Email Address Harvested
description: An employee email address was discovered via theHarvester, Hunter.io, LinkedIn, or public sources. Collected addresses support phishing and credential spray attacks.
remediation: Educate employees on minimising personal information exposure. Implement email security controls (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, anti-phishing).

title: Web Technology Fingerprint
description: The technology stack of a live host was identified (Wappalyzer, httpx, whatweb): CMS, web framework, server software, JavaScript libraries, CDN providers. Helps attackers target known vulnerabilities.
remediation: Remove version disclosure from HTTP headers (Server, X-Powered-By). Keep software up to date. Consider a WAF to obscure fingerprinting.

title: Wayback Machine URL with Sensitive Path
description: waybackurls or xurlfind3r discovered a historical URL containing a sensitive path (e.g., /admin, /backup, /.env, /config, /api/v1/keys) that was once publicly accessible.
remediation: Verify whether the resource still exists. Remove sensitive files from public-facing web roots. Review server access logs for recent access to these paths.

title: Shodan Exposure — Open Service
description: Shodan reports an open service on a target IP that is visible to the public internet. Banner data, software version, and service type are indexed and searchable by anyone.
remediation: Restrict access to services that do not need to be publicly reachable. Apply firewall rules. Update exposed services to current versions.

title: Shodan Exposure — Known CVE on Service
description: Shodan has associated one or more CVEs with a service running on a target IP based on the service banner and version string. A known public exploit may exist.
remediation: Patch or update the affected service immediately. If patching is not immediately possible, apply mitigating controls (WAF rule, network restriction).

title: Cloud Storage Bucket Found
description: cloud_enum or manual enumeration discovered a publicly accessible cloud storage bucket (AWS S3, Azure Blob, GCP Storage) associated with the target. It may contain sensitive files.
remediation: Immediately set the bucket to private unless public access is intentional. Audit bucket contents for sensitive data. Enable bucket access logging and alerts.

title: Certificate Transparency Log Entry
description: A certificate was found in CT logs (crt.sh, Certspotter, Facebook CT) for the target domain. The SAN/CN reveals subdomain names that may not be otherwise discoverable.
remediation: No direct remediation required. Review disclosed subdomains for unintended exposure. Consider certificate issuance monitoring for your domain.

title: ASN / IP Range Identified
description: The Autonomous System Number (ASN) and associated IP ranges for the target organisation were identified via BGP data and asnmap. This defines the full network footprint for scanning.
remediation: No immediate action required. Ensure only intended IP ranges are associated with the organisation's ASN. Review WHOIS/ARIN records for accuracy.

title: WHOIS Data Exposure
description: WHOIS records for the target domain revealed registrant contact details, nameserver names, registrar information, and registration dates. This information aids in phishing and social engineering.
remediation: Enable WHOIS privacy protection through your registrar for domains where registrant PII should not be public.

title: LinkedIn Employee Profile Enumerated
description: Employee names, titles, and organisational roles were enumerated from LinkedIn. This information supports spear-phishing, social engineering, and targeted credential spray attacks.
remediation: Educate staff on LinkedIn exposure. Implement strict email security (DMARC p=reject). Train employees to recognise spear-phishing.

title: Social Media Profile Linked to Employee
description: maigret discovered social media profiles (Twitter, GitHub, Reddit, etc.) linked to an employee username derived from their email address. May reveal personal information useful for social engineering.
remediation: Assess employee privacy settings. Provide training on personal operational security.

title: Sensitive File Found via Web Crawler
description: katana or xurlfind3r discovered a publicly accessible file containing potentially sensitive data: backup archives (.zip, .bak), configuration files (.env, .config), log files, or database dumps.
remediation: Remove the file from the web root immediately. Audit web server directory listings. Restrict access to backup and config files via .htaccess or server config.

title: HTTP Security Headers Missing
description: httpx detected missing security headers on a live host: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, or Referrer-Policy.
remediation: Add security headers to web server or application configuration. Verify with securityheaders.com.

title: Default Credentials on Web Service
description: A discovered web application or administrative panel (identified via technology fingerprinting) is known to ship with default credentials and no evidence of hardening was found.
remediation: Change default credentials immediately. Restrict admin panel access by source IP. Implement MFA for administrative interfaces.

title: Uncover / Internet-Wide Scan Engine Match
description: The uncover tool found the target in internet-wide scan engine results (Shodan, Censys, FOFA, Quake360, ZoomEye, CriminalIP). Services and their versions are publicly catalogued.
remediation: Review all indexed services. Remove unnecessary public exposure. Ensure indexed software versions are patched and up to date.

title: Wildcard DNS Record Detected
description: A wildcard DNS record (*.domain.com) was detected. This causes all subdomains to resolve, which may mask dangling CNAMEs and complicate subdomain takeover detection.
remediation: Remove wildcard records unless they serve a specific purpose. Document and review all subdomains that rely on wildcard resolution.

title: Cloud Service Provider Asset Identified
description: cloudlist or cdncheck identified assets hosted in cloud or CDN infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai). Provides context for attack surface mapping.
remediation: Ensure cloud-hosted assets have appropriate access controls, IAM policies, and logging. Review for misconfigured security groups or ACLs.

title: SEC EDGAR Filing Data Found
description: Public SEC EDGAR filings for the target company revealed corporate structure, subsidiary entities, executive names, and legal entity identifiers (LEI, CIK). Useful for targeted attacks and social engineering.
remediation: No direct remediation. Public regulatory filings are legally required for public companies. Ensure security awareness training covers executive impersonation risk.

title: Third-Party / Supply Chain Domain Identified
description: Enumeration revealed domains or subdomains associated with third-party services, SaaS providers, or supply chain vendors (identified via CNAME targets, MX records, or certificate SANs).
remediation: Maintain an inventory of third-party services. Assess vendor security posture. Monitor for supply chain compromise indicators.
